title: Why ice floats
source_text: When water freezes, its molecules lock into an open pattern that takes up more space than liquid water. This makes ice less dense, so it floats. Because of this, ponds freeze from the top down, and fish can survive the winter in the liquid water underneath the ice.

key_ideas.text: Water expands as it freezes, so ice is less dense than water and floats.
Ponds freeze from the top, so fish can survive in the water below the ice.

title: Why the sky is blue
source_text: Sunlight contains all the colours. As it passes through the air, blue light is scattered in every direction far more than red light, because blue light has a shorter wavelength. When we look at the sky away from the Sun, we are seeing this scattered blue light.

key_ideas.text: Air scatters blue light much more than red light because blue has a shorter wavelength.
The sky looks blue because we see this scattered blue light when looking away from the Sun.

title: Defrosting meat safely
source_text: The safest way to defrost meat is slowly in the fridge, which can take a day or more for a large joint. Defrosting at room temperature lets the outside warm up while the middle is still frozen, which gives bacteria on the surface time to multiply.

spoken_transcript: You should not defrost meat in the fridge; leaving it out at room temperature is the safest way.

title: Looking after a phone battery
source_text: Most phone batteries are lithium-ion. They tend to age more slowly if they are not kept at full charge for long periods or left somewhere hot, such as on a car dashboard. Letting the battery run completely flat on a regular basis is also unhelpful.

title: Hadrian's Wall
source_text: Hadrian's Wall was built by the Roman army from about AD 122, on the orders of the Emperor Hadrian. It ran for about 73 miles across northern England, from the River Tyne in the east to the Solway Firth in the west, with small forts called milecastles roughly every mile.

title: Dry stone walls
source_text: Dry stone walls are built without any mortar. Their strength comes from careful placing: the largest stones go at the bottom, the wall becomes narrower as it rises, and long through stones cross the full width to tie the two faces of the wall together.

key_ideas.text: Dry stone walls use no mortar; their strength comes from how the stones are placed.
Large stones go at the bottom, the wall narrows as it rises, and through stones tie both faces together.

spoken_transcript: No cement holds them up. Placement does: chunky stones low down, a gradually thinner wall as you go up, and lengthy stones spanning the whole width so both outer sides are bound to each other.

title: How owls fly quietly
source_text: Many owls have soft, fringed edges on their wing feathers. These fringes break up the rush of air over the wing and reduce the noise of flight. Flying quietly lets an owl hear small animals moving below and approach them without being noticed.

key_ideas.text: Soft, fringed feather edges reduce the noise of an owl's flight.
Quiet flight lets owls hear their prey and approach without being noticed.
